title: HMW DNA Extraction for Diatoms
author: Raffaela Abbriano
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.qzudx6w

steps.title: Harvest and wash diatom cells
steps.instruction: Collect 7 × 10⁷–2 × 10⁸ mid‑exponential‑phase cells, centrifuge at 5,000 × g for 3 min, discard supernatant, wash pellet once with 1 X PBS, centrifuge again at 5,000 × g for 3 min, and remove the supernatant.

steps.title: Cell lysis with freeze‑thaw and RNase
steps.instruction: Resuspend the washed pellet in 600 µL Nuclei Lysis Solution (Promega #A7941). Perform three freeze‑thaw cycles (freeze on dry ice or liquid N₂ for 3 min, thaw in a 65 °C heat block or water bath for 3 min or until fully thawed). After the cycles, heat the sample at 65 °C for 15 min, cool to room temperature, add 1.2 µL of 10 mg/mL RNase A (ThermoFisher #ENO531), incubate 15 min at 37 °C, then cool to room temperature. Use safe‑lock microcentrifuge tubes or lid locks during freeze‑thaw to prevent pressure‑related lid opening.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend cells in 600 µL Nuclei Lysis Solution (Promega #A7941).
Freeze on dry ice or liquid N₂ for 3 min.
Thaw in 65 °C block or water bath for 3 min (or until thawed).
Repeat freeze/thaw cycle total of 3 times.
Use lock‑cap tubes or lid locks (e.g., VWR lid locks) for safety.

steps.title: Protein precipitation and supernatant transfer
steps.instruction: Add 250 µL Protein Precipitation Solution (Promega #A7951) to the lysate, mix well, centrifuge at 16,000 × g for 40 min at 4 °C, then transfer the clear supernatant to a fresh tube.

substeps.instruction: Transfer supernatant to a new tube.

steps.title: DNA precipitation, wash, and resuspension
steps.instruction: To the transferred supernatant add 700 µL 100 % isopropanol, invert to mix, centrifuge at 16,000 × g for 30 min at room temperature, discard supernatant, wash the DNA pellet with 600 µL freshly prepared 70 % molecular‑grade ethanol, centrifuge 16,000 × g for 1 min, remove all ethanol (use a quick spin and a small pipette tip if needed), air‑dry the pellet 10–15 min, resuspend in 25–50 µL TE buffer (volume based on pellet size), let it sit at room temperature overnight for complete dissolution, then determine concentration with a Nanodrop. Note: after isopropanol precipitation the pellet may appear as a translucent smear; it becomes a visible white pellet after the ethanol wash.

substeps.instruction: Wash pellet with 600 µL 70 % ethanol (molecular grade, freshly prepared).
Remove all ethanol (quick spin, small tip if needed).
Incubate at RT overnight for complete dissolution.
Observe pellet appearance: translucent after isopropanol, white after ethanol wash.

steps.title: DNA quantification and agarose gel analysis
steps.instruction: Load 100–200 ng of the purified DNA onto a 0.8 % agarose gel, run the gel, and compare band patterns to a ladder (top band ≈ 40 kb) to assess high‑molecular‑weight DNA quality.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 0.8 % agarose gel with appropriate ladder.
Visualize bands and record yields (e.g., Thalassiosira pseudonana 1255.8 ng/µL, 260/280 = 1.8, 260/230 = 1.86, etc.).
